content: Returns & Refunds Service — Requirements Specification
Version 3.1 — 12 June 2025
rationale: version/date stamp; could be read as document control

content: Document ID: RR-SPEC-031 | Status: Approved | Review date: 2025-12-01
Return merchandise authorization (RMA): A unique code issued by the system that authorizes a customer to send an item back.
Restocking fee: A percentage of the item price withheld from a refund when a returned item has been opened.
rationale: definition that embeds a rule-like clause

content: The system shall allow a customer to initiate a return from the order history page for any delivered order.
The system shall issue an RMA code and display it to the customer after a return is submitted.
Given a return has been marked as received, when a warehouse operator confirms inspection, then the system shall issue a refund to the original payment method.
The system shall send the customer a confirmation email containing the RMA code within 1 minute of return submission.
The system shall prevent a return from being initiated for an order that has not yet been delivered.
Customers can filter their return history by status (pending, received, refunded).
Items may be returned within 30 days of delivery.
Final-sale items are not eligible for return.
Opened electronics are subject to a 15% restocking fee.
Refunds are issued to the original payment method only; store credit may not be substituted without the customer's consent.
Return shipping is free for defective items and paid by the customer in all other cases.

Item category | Return window | Restocking fee
Apparel | 30 days | None
Electronics | 30 days | 15% if opened
Furniture | 14 days | 20%

Role | Permission
Customer | Initiate return
Warehouse operator | Confirm receipt
Finance | Approve refunds over $500
rationale: permission matrix; could be read as testable behaviour

content: For example, a customer who received a $200 opened laptop on 1 March and returns it on 20 March is refunded $170, because the 15% restocking fee ($30) applies.
Example: an order delivered on 1 May can be returned until 31 May; a return initiated on 1 June is rejected.
Scenario: a customer returns two of three items from one order. Only the two returned items are refunded; the original shipping charge is not refunded.
Revision history: v3.0 (2025-04-02) added restocking fee; v3.1 (2025-06-12) clarified final-sale items.
Reviewers: Dana Whitfield (Finance), Luis Ortega (Support), Mei Chen (Legal).
This document is confidential and intended solely for internal use by Acme Corp employees.
Out of scope for this release: international returns and customs documentation.
rationale: explicit scope exclusion; mentions rules but is not testable

Customers see an inline error message when they enter an expired or unrecognised discount code.
Given a cart subtotal of $5.00, when the customer submits a discount code, then the system displays an error and leaves the total unchanged.
The checkout summary page shall render within 2 seconds at the 95th percentile under the documented load profile.
The system shall not store the full card number after payment authorization completes.
The system shall recalculate the order total whenever the quantity of a line item changes.
Discount codes shall not be combined with any other promotion on the same order.
Gift cards are not subject to sales tax.
Note: shipping charges are excluded from the amount that a discount code reduces.

Subtotal range | Shipping charge
$0.00–$49.99 | $5.99
$50.00 and above | Free
Each customer may hold at most one active promotional code at a time.
A $50.00 cart with a valid 20% code totals $40.00; the same cart with a 10% code totals $45.00.
Entering the code SAVE99 on the cart page displays the message "SAVE99 is not a valid discount code."
Suppose a customer has two Widgets at $30.00 each and one Sticker at $5.00. The subtotal is $65.00 before any discount.
A SKU (stock keeping unit) is the unique identifier a merchant assigns to each purchasable product variant.
Subtotal — the sum of line-item prices before discounts, tax and shipping.
The system shall be built and maintained in accordance with the company's secure coding standards.
rationale: uses 'shall' but nothing testable at the feature level

content: Future releases may add support for gift cards and loyalty points; these are not covered by this specification.

content: Checkout Service — Requirements Specification, Version 1.1 (2025-03-05)
Page 5 of 8 — Checkout Service Requirements — Internal
The system shall sign users out automatically and redirect them to the login page when their session expires.
The system shall reject passwords shorter than 12 characters and display the reason.
Passwords must be at least 12 characters long and may not contain the user's email address.
Given a locked account, when the lockout period elapses, then the user can log in again with valid credentials.
The system shall not reveal whether an email address is registered when a login attempt fails.
Administrator accounts are exempt from the idle timeout while a privileged operation is in progress.
Each user may have at most 5 concurrent active sessions.
A user who has been idle since 10:00 and returns at 10:45 is redirected to the login page and must sign in again.
Entering a wrong password on the login page shows "Invalid email or password" and does not indicate which field was wrong.
rationale: concrete case; could be read as acceptance criterion

content: Authenticator app: A mobile application that generates time-based one-time passcodes (TOTP) used as a second authentication factor.
Lockout window refers to the 15-minute period during which failed login attempts are counted.
rationale: definition phrased with 'refers to'; also carries a number

content: Single sign-on with external identity providers is out of scope for this release.
